comments.author: @tanyawales5445
comments.text:
There is no specific chemical spray used to make strawberries unnaturally huge. Instead, their large size is the result of careful plant breeding, optimized fertilizers, and strict growing conditions.

Farmers utilize specific methods to maximize berry size:

Variety Selection: Breeders intentionally develop specific strawberry cultivars (like the Albion or Monterey varieties) that are genetically predisposed to produce larger, firmer fruits.

Hydroponics & Fertilizers: Growers use precise hydroponic systems or soil-based nutrient schedules—feeding the plants exact ratios of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium—to encourage robust cell division and fruit growth.

Selective Pruning: Growers may nip the first few flowers off a young plant during its first season. This forces the plant to channel all its energy into root development and producing larger, higher-quality berries later on.
